ai.description: *Eutropis clivicola* (Scincidae) reaches 7 cm snout-vent length. It is bronze-brown with a distinct pale dorsolateral stripe and dark lateral bands. It features smooth scales and a pointed snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Eutropis clivicola* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark mid-lateral stripe that remains unbroken and clearly defined along the length of its body.
ai.habitat: *Eutropis clivicola* inhabits moist deciduous forests and evergreen forest edges in the Western Ghats, typically found at mid-to-high elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Eutropis clivicola* is a diurnal skink that actively forages for small invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky outcrops during the warmest parts of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eutropis clivicola* is viviparous, typically producing a litter of 3–5 young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eutropis clivicola* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
